nodes.label: ADR 0017: diacritic CLI imports BT variants as their own index entries
nodes.rationale: After ADR 0016 nothing repeatable added Bosworth-Toller variants; the 462 variants already present came from a throwaway script. A dry-run-by-default importer stores each variant as its own lowercase entry using the spelling BT prints, never copies headword marks onto a different spelling, and never changes an existing key. Frontmatter remains proposed; the body says the importer is implemented and the packaged index has not been imported yet. Storing BT diphthong style is safe only because ADR 0020 treats a diphthong as one unit.

nodes.label: diacritic import-variants
nodes.rationale: The command makes the ADR 0016 repair repeatable. It reads oe_bt.txt, adds each kept variant as its own top-level key, dry-runs by default, and writes a JSON review report. Existing keys are never changed: same or fewer marks are skipped, richer or conflicting marks are reported, and ambiguous_completed keys are never touched. There is no --variant-of flag because the index has no headword link.

nodes.label: BT variant import pipeline
nodes.rationale: BTLineParser.raw_variants must supply un-normalized headwords and variants. ParsedBTLine.variants already passed through BTSpellingNormalizer, which would violate the rule to store what BT prints. BTVariantFilter and BTVariantImporter live in wyrdcraeft.services; report models live in wyrdcraeft.models.variant_import; the command is in wyrdcraeft.cli.diacritic.

nodes.label: BT variant junk filter and similarity gate
nodes.rationale: A minimum length would drop the real word aa, a variant of ā. Hard rejects instead drop keys that occur under three or more headwords, a hand-edited stoplist, ALL-CAPS tokens, and hyphenated fragments whose last segment is one letter. A similarity gate then auto-imports only variants within max(2, len(headword key) // 3) edits of the headword. Inflected forms and English note-words cannot be separated without an English word list, so they go to review.

nodes.label: bt_variant_stoplist.txt
nodes.rationale: The stoplist holds citation sigla and Roman numerals that the frequency rule misses. It is hand-edited and extended as review reports show more junk. The edit-distance gate still admits some three-letter noise, and lowering the distance to 1 would drop genuine dialect spellings, so the stoplist is the escape hatch.
